## Why the refusals are what they are

Each of these is a protocol fact, not a to-do item. A row that reads `N` here does not become
`p` by writing more code — it needs a different browser or a different transport.

- **`firefox` · `accessibilityTree`** — status `UNSUPPORTED` via bidi: WebDriver BiDi defines no accessibility module, and Firefox 129 removed CDP. No transport carries an AX tree to us.
  - recorded reason: *WebDriver BiDi defines no accessibility module, so there is no tree to ask for*
- **`firefox` · `screenshotFullPage`** — status `UNSUPPORTED` via bidi: BiDi capture is viewport-only; full-page was still an open specification issue when the draft was read.
  - recorded reason: *BiDi capture is viewport-only; full-page was still an open specification issue when read*
- **`safari` · `attachToRunning`** — status `UNSUPPORTED` via safaridriver: safaridriver is a W3C WebDriver server; it exposes no endpoint for a browser that is already open.
  - recorded reason: *safaridriver is a W3C WebDriver server; it does not expose an attach endpoint for a running browser*
- **`safari` · `accessibilityTree`** — status `UNSUPPORTED` via safaridriver: W3C WebDriver defines no accessibility tree at all.
  - recorded reason: *W3C WebDriver defines no accessibility tree*
- **`chrome` · `websockets`** — status `UNSUPPORTED` via cdp: This process cannot route WebSocket frames through its own SSRF check because the driver layer does not expose them. Reported as unsupported rather than silently unproxied.
  - recorded reason: *this process cannot route WebSocket frames through the SSRF check: the driver layer does not expose them. Documented in pinned-proxy.ts.*
- **`arc` · `launch`** — status `UNKNOWN` via cdp: Arc ships a Chromium core with no documented remote-debugging interface. `?`, not `p`: nobody has made it start.
  - recorded reason: *Arc ships a Chromium core but no documented debugging endpoint; not verified here*
